audit_scope: Definition-level comparison of the pinned Formal Conjectures P != NP statement and its imported Lean definitions against the protected Programme machine, encoding, totality, uniformity, and polynomial-bound lock.

checks.finding: ComplexityTheory.P_ne_NP has the separation orientation and can address only the P != NP side of the Programme terminal alternatives.
The imported declaration ends with `by sorry`; it is a conjectural statement candidate and supplies no proof or certification evidence.

The upstream carrier is a total Boolean-valued function on List Bool; the Programme carrier is a language over binary strings. The true-preimage correspondence is standard but no pinned Lean equivalence theorem connects the two class presentations.
finEncodingListBool is the identity encoding on finite Boolean lists, so the upstream input measure is exactly encoded bit-list length.
TM2ComputableInPolyTime requires an Option.some encoded output for every input within the polynomial bound; P and the NP verifier are total Boolean functions.
Every List Bool is a valid class-level input. The Programme malformed-to-NO convention remains an obligation for any concrete SAT or other encoded endpoint and is not discharged by P_ne_NP.
Membership uses one finite FinTM2 description for all inputs; no advice string, per-length circuit family, oracle, or noncomputable parameter is present in the imported definition.

The upstream deterministic finite multi-stack TM2 model is documented as classically equivalent, while the Programme lock uses a deterministic multitape Turing machine. This package found no pinned kernel-checked polynomial-simulation bridge between those presentations.

The upstream bound is evaluation of a Polynomial Nat at encoded input length; the Programme accepts a worst-case c*n^k or n^k+k bound. Their class-level equivalence is expected but not imported as a proved conversion theorem.

The upstream NP definition uses a deterministic polynomial-time Boolean verifier and a Polynomial Nat witness-length bound, with a delimiter-based finite encoding of the input-witness pair. A class-extensional proof against the Programme verifier presentation is still absent.
P_ne_NP is a class inequality and contains no SAT language, parser, polynomial many-one reduction, or endpoint correctness theorem. Those obligations remain mandatory for a concrete terminal route.

open_bridges.obligation: Prove an extensional equivalence between Boolean-valued decision problems and Programme languages over binary strings, preserving class equality and inequality.
Provide a pinned polynomial-overhead simulation theorem between the upstream finite TM2 model and the Programme deterministic multitape Turing-machine model.
Prove both conversions between Polynomial Nat evaluation bounds and the Programme worst-case asymptotic polynomial bounds, including all input lengths.
Prove class-extensional equivalence of the upstream deterministic-verifier NP definition, pair encoding, and witness bound with the Programme NP lock.
For any concrete NP-complete endpoint, bind parsing, malformed-to-NO behavior, total correctness, encoded size, and the locked polynomial many-one reductions.
